## Natural history notes

A crust-like wood-decay fungus characterized by thin, flat patches on dead wood with pale whitish to tan areas mixed with warmer reddish-brown or orangish spotting, giving it the “giraffe spots” appearance. In Florida, it grows on dead hardwood branches, fallen limbs, logs, and woody debris in hammocks, hardwood forests, mixed woods, parks, and shaded yards. It acts as a decomposer, breaking down dead wood and helping recycle nutrients while creating microhabitat for tiny insects, mites, springtails, and other wood-associated organisms.
